title: Audio Generation — Codec Tokens and Style-Conditioned Sequences

questions.question: How does make_tokens(style=0, length=4, rng) define its synthetic speech-like sequence?
options: It uses (i + random bit) % 16 for each position
It uses (3*i + random bit) % 16 for each position
It draws every token uniformly from 0 through 4
It repeats the start token four times
questions.explanation: The style-0 branch returns `[(i + rng.randint(0,1)) % VOCAB ...]` with VOCAB=16; style 1 uses the three-step ramp.

questions.question: What does init_counts create before any token sequences are observed?
options: A [16][2] one-hot table with all rows zero
A [2][16][16] table filled with 1.0 transition counts
One scalar count per style and no previous-token dimension
A probability table with exactly one successor per token
questions.explanation: The nested comprehension allocates one 16-by-16 transition table for each of the two styles and initializes every cell to 1.0.

questions.question: How does update_counts use a sequence [a,b,c] for one style?
options: It adds the sequence length to every vocabulary row
It increments only counts[style][c][a]
It increments counts[style][a][b] and counts[style][b][c]
It replaces the row for a with a one-hot vector for c
questions.explanation: The loop visits adjacent pairs with `range(len(sequence)-1)` and increments the transition from each token to the next.

questions.question: What does probs(counts, style, prev_tok) guarantee about its returned row?
options: It samples a token immediately and returns its integer ID
Only the most frequent next token has probability one
It returns raw counts whose sum depends on training volume
The probabilities sum to one after dividing the selected count row by its total
questions.explanation: The helper selects one style/previous-token row, sums it, and divides every entry by that total.

questions.question: For temperature=0.7, how does generate transform a transition row before sampling?
options: It raises each probability to 1/0.7 and renormalizes, sharpening relative differences
It multiplies every probability by 0.7 without renormalizing
It discards all tokens except the largest row index
It adds 0.7 to every token count after sampling
questions.explanation: The code applies `pi ** (1 / temperature)` and then divides by the new total; temperatures below one make the distribution more peaked.

questions.question: Why does the VALL-E-style continuation keep the five prompt tokens before generating 15 more?
options: The prompt is discarded after its last token is read
The final prompt token supplies the initial context while the existing prompt remains part of the returned sequence
Each prompt token is converted into a separate style model
The continuation length is always equal to the prompt length
questions.explanation: main copies `prompt` into continuation and appends one sampled token per step, preserving the five-token acoustic prompt.
